oil.summary: Crude edged marginally higher on the day — WTI +0.13% to $68.78, Brent +0.46% to $72.13 — but the one-month collapse of roughly 27-28% dominates the picture. The structural bearish driver is clear: the UAE, following its OPEC exit, ramped production above 3.8 mb/d in June, adding supply pressure the market is struggling to absorb. Russian Urals has crashed to ~$41.66/bbl, erasing the war premium accumulated during the Iran conflict. Ukrainian drone strikes on a Crimean tanker and the St. Petersburg oil terminal are keeping a geopolitical floor under prices without materially tightening supply. Iran's ongoing blockade posture and Trump's reported consideration of seizing Iranian oil add headline risk. Refined products outperformed sharply — Heating Oil +2.34%, RBOB +1.23% — suggesting some near-term crack spread support.
drivers: UAE post-OPEC exit production surge to 3.8 mb/d adds significant supply, compounding month-long price rout
Urals crashes to ~$41.66/bbl as Ukraine drone strikes degrade Russian export infrastructure at St. Petersburg and Crimea
Iran blockade and Trump's threat to seize Iranian cargoes maintain geopolitical risk premium; options market prices 77% probability of further OPEC cuts at next meeting
sources: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos

gas.summary: Henry Hub edged up 1.53% to $3.245/MMBtu, extending a modest but steady recovery with the one-month gain now nearly 1%. TTF added 0.53% to €44.25/MWh, though the more significant story is the 8.5% weekly surge in European gas, likely reflecting residual Hormuz/LNG supply anxiety. Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is described as recovering but still disrupted, with at least six LNG-carrying vessels affected by persistent risks. Russia's retaliatory strikes on Ukrainian gas sites add supply-side concern for European flows. News flow for this sector today is relatively thin beyond these two drivers; the Iran-war renewables-investment narrative is forward-looking rather than an immediate price catalyst.
drivers: Hormuz tanker traffic recovering slowly but LNG disruptions persist, supporting TTF's sharp 8.5% weekly gain
Russia strikes Ukrainian gas infrastructure in retaliation, raising near-term European supply-continuity concerns
Henry Hub holding a modest positive trend; broader gas news flow today is limited

power.summary: EU Carbon (EUA) continued its grind higher, up 1.59% on the day to $77.53/EUA, with a +6.56% one-month gain standing in stark contrast to the crude selloff. A headline noting carbon markets have reached what is described as their most important credibility inflection point in years may be supporting sentiment. On the demand side, India's power consumption is projected to grow ~6% annually through 2030, with a Super El Niño expected to accelerate coal-fired generation over the next 12 months — a bearish clean-energy signal but bullish for carbon pricing. The UK's estimated £500bn net-zero bill is flagged as a potential competitiveness risk. North America reportedly drove nearly half of global emissions growth in 2025, per the Energy Institute's 2026 Statistical Review.
drivers: EUA carbon prices up 1.59% on the day and +6.57% on the month, bolstered by reported credibility milestone in carbon markets
India Super El Niño expected to lift coal-fired power demand materially over next 12 months; India power demand seen growing 6%/yr to 2030
North America accounted for nearly half of global emissions growth in 2025 per Energy Institute; UK faces $667bn net-zero bill flagged as competitiveness risk
